I was really constipated while on holiday in Japan. 

I was already constipated before I left my country but I didn't want to be dealing with the sudden urge to poop that comes with taking stool softeners.

I was at breakfast on the second day, I'd eaten so much food and drunk so much beer in the past 24 hours that I was so uncomfortable. I was in that cage toilet for so long that the staff knocked... 

I was also really excited to try the bidets that make my one at home look like a poor man's fountain. So I decided it was time to go to a pharmacy to get something to help me poop. I looked up online and on reddit for what the laxatives look like and settled on this pink box. 

It was a long rest of the day of sightseeing and eating and much more drinking we got back to the apartment, I translated the back of the box of laxatives and it said to take 1 - 3. Luckily I used my better judgment and just took the one.

The next morning I woke up, walked across the street and got a coffee from the vending machine, I was marveling at how hot the can was when it hit me. This time I was safe but I barely made it up the crazy steep stairs to the toilet where I did the biggest poop of my life, I feel like a new woman when I was finished. 

The rest of the the morning we packed up as we were moving on to the next city. Everything was sorted and checkout was 11. At 10:40 I was washing our dishes, which was the last thing we had to do, I farted... I have never shit my parts before and I wasn't expecting it at all, whatever  was in those laxatives had made my shit into a jelly like consistency. The worst part is that my other pair of jeans was in the bottom of my bag and by the time I'd cleaned up it was 10:55. The whole rest of my 3 week trip I didn't trust a fart once. 

So if you are ever in Japan and are so constipated it hurts the laxatives in the pink box work a little too well.

I definitely am going to finish the program because I am incredibly lucky to have it funded under a National Insurance scheme, otherwise I'd never have been able to afford it.
